historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026/27 organic sales guidance (~5%) cross-checked against the 3-year revenue CAGR of 5.1% (FY2023-FY2026, the clean post-Bombardier window) and a EUR104bn backlog covering 5.4x sales with FY26 book-to-bill 1.44x
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Historical CAGRs are structurally unreliable for this ticker: (1) the 5-year revenue CAGR of 16.9% spans the Jan-2021 Bombardier acquisition (FY2021 revenue 8,785 -> FY2022 15,471) and is not organic; (2) equity CAGRs (5.8% / 3.4%) are inflated by the 2021 Bombardier share issuance, the 2024 EUR1bn rights issue and the EUR750m hybrid, not by retained earnings - cumulative FY2022-FY2024 net losses were EUR1.0bn; (3) EPS 3-year CAGR is undefined (FY2023 EPS -0.35) and the 5-year figure is negative; (4) the owner-FCF 3-year CAGR of 34.5% runs from a depressed FY2023 base of 133 (reported 199 - SBC 66) to FY2026 324 (336 - 12), and lease principal is not separately available across the history, so the series is reported FCF less SBC rather than the full treatment-(B) owner FCF. None of these is used as the growth input; guidance plus backlog coverage is.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported company FCF less SBC, EUR m): FY2017 172, FY2018 108, FY2019 131, FY2020 181, FY2021 -713, FY2022 -1,034, FY2023 133, FY2024 -576, FY2025 482, FY2026 324. Three of the last six years were cash-negative, which is why the scenario weights carry a 30% bear.

scenario_narratives.base: Alstom delivers FY2026/27 roughly as guided - ~5% organic growth, aEBIT margin ~6.5%, positive FCF after the ~EUR1.5bn H1 seasonal consumption - and the new CEO's operational plan then lifts the margin about 30bp a year to 7.8% by FY2032, the bottom of the old 8-10% ambition but never its midpoint. Growth decelerates from the EUR104bn backlog (5.4x sales) toward 2.5% as book-to-bill normalises to ~1.0-1.1x. Capex, including capitalised R&D, runs 3.1% of sales on the car-production ramp (4,400-4,500 cars) and settles at 2.7%; working capital consumes 10% of each euro of growth because milestone cash lags production. Restructuring cash tapers from 0.35% to 0.2% of sales as the German footprint consolidation completes. Cash tax ramps from 24% to 27%. The axes that matter: whether the 18.0% gross margin in backlog converts at the project level, and whether contract working capital stops absorbing cash as the ramp matures.
scenario_narratives.bull: The early-2027 Capital Markets Day re-validates an 8-10% aEBIT margin with a credible site-by-site industrialisation plan and the market gives Martin Sion the benefit of the doubt. Record FY26 order intake (EUR27.6bn, +90% rolling stock, US wins at LIRR/Metro-North and NJ Transit) lifts growth to 6-6.5% for two years; the margin reaches 9.2% by FY2033 as the Services/Signalling mix rises and PPA-era footprint costs roll off; down payments on new orders fund the ramp so working capital is neutral to growth. Terminal growth 2.5% on the secular rail/decarbonisation tailwind. Value is in the flows; the WACC is unchanged.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY2025/26 pattern repeats: industrialisation of flagship platforms and homologation slip again, a further project charge takes FY2026/27 aEBIT to ~6.0% and the margin never clears 6.5%; restructuring stays a permanent ~EUR70m/yr line. FX (USD, CAD, GBP, INR), Middle East backlog (2-3% of sales) and public-budget delays hold growth to ~2%, and working capital absorbs 25 cents of every euro of growth as the FY27 H1 EUR1.5bn consumption proves less seasonal than guided. The balance sheet survives - net debt 404m, Baa3 stable - so this is a value-trap outcome, not a distress one; a Moody's downgrade constraining bonding capacity is the tail beyond this path.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Alstom is valued as a long-cycle rail OEM whose equity value hinges almost entirely on converting a record, higher-margin backlog into cash at a margin it has so far failed to reach. The flows are unlevered owner FCF anchored on the company's own cash EBITDA (EBIT before PPA + D&A + JV dividends, 1,502 in FY26, not the 1,728 that aEBIT + D&A would imply): SBC expensed, lease cash charged inside EBITDA (so leases are not in net debt), restructuring/integration/other and the non-cash JV pick-up treated as recurring, and cash tax ramped to a normal rate. Debt-like claims the IFRS statements keep out of net debt - the EUR750m hybrid, EUR635m pension deficit, NCI at fair value - are deducted in the bridge. One EUR WACC of 8.5% across scenarios, with execution risk carried by the driver paths and a 30% bear weight, and a 15x terminal cap because this is a cyclical, thin-margin manufacturer, not a compounder.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin path: every 1pt of terminal aEBIT margin is worth roughly EUR4-5/share; the base assumes 7.8% against a FY26 actual of 6.1% and guidance of ~6.5%
Working capital: contract WC swung -290 in FY26 and H1 FY27 is guided at -1.5bn; a structural rather than seasonal consumption would pull every scenario toward the bear

Below-aEBIT leakage: restructuring, integration and 'other' have cost EUR160-220m/yr every year since 2021 and the JV pick-up exceeds JV dividends by ~70m; the base tapers the former to 0.4% of sales but a company that keeps reporting 'non-recurring' items is worth the bear path
Project charges: a single large fixed-price contract overrun (FY24-style) can erase a year of FCF; the model carries restructuring but no explicit charge provision
Bridge judgments: NCI at 10x earnings (410) rather than book (121), pensions at 635, and the 656 net DTA not credited together move the value ~EUR1.5/share; all are stated
Lease approximation: ROU depreciation is proxied by the 172 principal repayment; a materially different split would move the tax line, not the cash flows
Bombardier PPA amortisation (~250m/yr) is non-cash and excluded; if the market keeps valuing on reported EPS the re-rating may lag the cash

data_sources.financials: research/ALO.PA/Reports/ALO.PA_Metrics.csv and the kpis table (AdjustedEBIT, ReportedFreeCashFlow, Backlog, OrderIntake, CashTaxesPaid), both derived from ALO.PA_Annual_FY2017-FY2026.txt (Universal Registration Documents); FY2025/26 URD sections 2.10.9 (net debt), 2.10.13 (EV-to-equity bridge), notes 10 (diluted shares), 27 (lease obligations and interest), 30 (share-based payments), cash flow statement (capex incl. capitalised R&D, lease principal); ALO.PA_Quarterly_Q1-2027.txt (July 2026 outlook confirmation)

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 462,029,966 shares on issue at 31 March 2026 plus 3,462,603 dilutive LTI performance shares/options (URD FY2025/26 note 10, diluted weighted average 465,362,712). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows (EUR12m, 0.06% of sales), so dilution is charged once. The 2024 rights issue (+~84m shares) and the EUR750m hybrid are already in the count and the bridge respectively; no further non-SBC issuance is assumed.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company definition (URD 2.10.9): cash 2,297 + other current financial assets 60 (net of EUR26m NMTC deposit) less current financial debt 781 and non-current financial debt 1,980 = net debt 404 at 31 March 2026 (434 at 31 March 2025). Lease obligations of 795 are EXCLUDED here because the lease cash is charged inside the flows (treatment B). The EUR750m deeply subordinated perpetual (hybrid) is equity under IFRS and is therefore not in this figure; it is deducted in equity_bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: URD FY2025/26 cash flow statement, 'Expense arising from share-based payments' EUR12m (FY2024/25 EUR20m); note 30. No cash taxes on net-share settlement disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 in kpis).
inputs.last_fcf_note: Unlevered owner FCF under lease treatment (B): company FCF 336 (OCF 891 - capex incl. capitalised R&D 567 + disposals 13) - SBC 12 - lease principal 172 (lease interest 34 is already inside the company figure) + net interest paid on borrowings 22 (the model is unlevered; debt and hybrid are charged in the bridge) = 174. Interest income (EUR30-39m) is NOT stripped: Alstom is a net debtor, so the cash pile is not double-counted via the bridge.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases in any year FY2017-FY2026 (financing activities). The flat count is a modelling convention, not something the company funds; dilution from LTI grants (~0.7%/yr) is instead charged as the SBC expense in the flows.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in EUR, the currency of the flows: 10y OAT ~3.3% risk-free, 5.5% equity risk premium, beta ~1.4 (the stock has traded 14.5-30.2 over 52 weeks and halved on a single margin cut) -> cost of equity ~11%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.0% (Baa3 stable / BBB-), ~3.0% after tax. Target capital structure ~30% debt-like claims (borrowings + hybrid + leases ~4.3bn against ~7.5bn market cap today, falling as net debt is repaid) -> WACC 0.70 x 11 + 0.30 x 3.0 = 8.4%, rounded to 8.5%. ONE rate across all three scenarios: execution, margin and working-capital risk are priced in the scenario flows and the 30% bear weight, not stacked in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. FY2025/26 lease cash = principal repayments EUR172m (financing, 'Changes in lease obligations') + interest on lease obligations EUR34m (operating, note 27 footnote 2) = EUR206m = 1.07% of sales, carried as lease_cost_pct_path ~1.05%. Lease obligations (EUR795m, of which EUR44m train leases matched by a financial asset) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A for cash tax is ex right-of-use depreciation: D&A before PPA 560 less ROU depreciation (approximated by the 172 principal repayment) = 388 = 2.02% of sales. Charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI charged once, in the bridge, at an estimated fair value rather than book: FY2025/26 net profit attributable to NCI was EUR41m against a book NCI of EUR121m, so book materially understates the claim. Deducted at 10x NCI earnings = EUR410m (about EUR0.9/share; the company's own EV-to-equity bridge uses book 121). Flows are left on a 100% consolidated basis.
inputs.ebitda_definition: ebitda_margin_path is the engine's EBITDA, anchored on the company's own cash starting point in URD 2.6: 'EBITDA before PPA + JV dividends' = EBIT before PPA 797 + D&A before PPA 560 + JV dividends 145 = 1,502, plus the SBC expense 12 that the engine deducts separately = 1,514 = 7.90% of sales for FY2025/26. This is BELOW aEBIT + D&A (1,728) by design: aEBIT 1,168 includes EUR216m of non-cash equity-investee pick-up (mostly Chinese JVs; cash dividends were 145, so 71 is non-cash), EUR56m restructuring, EUR106m 'integration costs, impairment and other' and +7 disposal gains, all of which recur every year since the 2021 acquisition (FY25: 148 pick-up vs 156 dividends, 16 restructuring, 202 integration/other). Engine EBIT = 7.90 - 0.06 SBC - 1.07 lease - 2.02 D&A ex-ROU = 4.75% = 911m; cash taxes paid 241 are 26.5% of that, which is what the tax path starts from. Modelled FY26 owner FCF on these inputs is ~324 vs actual unlevered owner FCF 174; the residual ~150 is hedging costs, pension contributions and provision timing inside 'financial and tax cash-out' and is treated as noise, not a recurring line. Bombardier PPA amortisation (~EUR250m/yr, running off) is non-cash and excluded. Forward translation: engine EBITDA = aEBIT path + D&A pre-PPA (da_pct + 0.9pt ROU) + 0.07 SBC - 0.30 JV non-cash gap - restructuring/integration/other (0.80 tapering to 0.40 base, 0.30 bull; 0.85 flat bear).
inputs.tax_note: Book effective tax rate is 'n.m.' / 64-73% because losses in some jurisdictions carry no recognised deferred tax asset; it is not a forecasting input. Cash taxes paid were EUR241m in FY2025/26 = 26.5% of modelled unlevered engine EBIT (911m) and 21% of aEBIT (1,168m). Base path runs the cash rate 25% -> 27% (French statutory 25.8%, blended group ~27%); bear 26% -> 28%. The EUR656m net recognised DTA in the company's bridge is NOT added back (conservative).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year explicit horizon (margins still ramping at year 5), with the non-US/cyclical adaptations: EUR-built WACC, lease treatment (B), NCI in the bridge, hybrid and pensions as debt-like claims, matching-asset rule applied (Chinese JV income stays in aEBIT so Chinese JVs stay OUT of the bridge; associates ex-China and non-consolidated investments are added because their income is below aEBIT). First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry). WHY THIS MODEL: Alstom is an operating rail OEM whose value is a stream of project and services cash flow; the Jan-2021 Bombardier Transportation acquisition doubled the group (revenue 8.8bn -> 15.5bn, backlog 40.9bn -> 74.5bn), so pre-FY2022 history is a different company and the forward build anchors on FY2025/26 actuals and FY2026/27 guidance (organic growth ~5%, aEBIT margin ~6.5%, positive FCF after ~EUR1.5bn H1 consumption; confirmed July 2026). BASE-YEAR CHOICE: FY2025/26 is used because the balance-sheet repair is complete (net debt 404 vs ~3bn peak) and it is the first clean post-disposal year (signalling sale to Knorr-Bremse closed Sept 2024); the FY2024 FCF of -557 and FY2025 FCF of +502 are both distorted by the rights issue / disposal year and are not repeatable bases either way. Working capital is modelled on the CHANGE in revenue with NEGATIVE capture in base and bear (ramp-up of record orders consumes cash before milestones, as the FY26 contract WC of -290 and the guided H1 FY27 -1.5bn show), zero in bull (down payments on record order intake fund the ramp). SBC-light market: house and street values nearly coincide; band_position will be close to degenerate and should be read as such. Price is a Friday regular close, not after-hours. Half-year FY2026/27 results (due ~mid-November 2026) will refresh net debt and the H1 cash consumption; the Capital Markets Day in early 2027 is the event that would move the margin paths.

bear.narrative: Implied aEBIT margin 6.0, 5.8, 6.0, 6.2, 6.3, 6.5 then flat at 6.5%, with restructuring/integration/other held at the FY26 0.85% of sales: a third margin miss in FY2026/27 (flagship platform industrialisation slips again), growth falls to ~2% as FX and public-budget delays bite, and working capital consumes 25% of each euro of growth. Not a solvency scenario - net debt is 404m against 2.3bn of cash - which is why the bear weight is 30% rather than 35%+.

base.narrative: Implied aEBIT margin path 6.5, 6.8, 7.1, 7.4, 7.6, 7.8 then flat at 7.8%. Engine EBITDA = aEBIT + D&A pre-PPA (da_pct + ~0.9pt ROU depreciation) + SBC 0.07 - 0.30 non-cash JV pick-up in excess of dividends - restructuring/integration/other tapering 0.80 -> 0.40. Reaches the bottom of the withdrawn 8-10% ambition only in year 6 and never the midpoint. Year-1 unlevered owner FCF ~EUR0.45bn (~2.2% of sales), i.e. roughly EUR0.6bn on the company's levered definition after adding back lease principal and deducting interest - consistent with 'positive FCF' guidance for FY2026/27 after the H1 EUR1.5bn consumption.

bull.narrative: Implied aEBIT margin 6.6, 7.2, 7.8, 8.4, 8.8, 9.0, 9.2 then flat, with restructuring/integration/other tapering 0.80 -> 0.30 and the 0.30 non-cash JV pick-up gap held: the early-2027 Capital Markets Day re-validates 8-10% and execution delivers the midpoint by year 7, converting the 18.0% backlog gross margin. Same WACC as base: the upside is in the flows, not a cheaper discount rate.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 30/50/20. Bear up: the margin ambition has been missed twice (FY26 actual 6.1% vs ~7% guided; 8-10% medium-term withdrawn to a 2027 CMD), the CEO is new with no rail background, and three of the last six years were cash-negative - but not 35%+, because net debt of 404m against 2.3bn cash and a stable Baa3 rating take solvency off the table. Bull down: it needs several independent things - CMD validation, project-level margin conversion, working capital turning neutral and sustained 6% growth - to go right together.
probability_weighted.band_position_note: SBC is 0.06% of sales, so house and street values differ by ~EUR0.5/share and the band_position the engine reports is degenerate (price far below both ends of a near-zero-width band). Read it as n/a, as in an SBC-zero market: the valuation does not depend on SBC treatment.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
